newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Amuay refinery repairs on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Amuay refinery repairs on schedule.

text.p: Repairs on a catalytic cracker unit at PdVSA affiliate Lagoven's 510,000 barrels per day (bpd) Amauy refinery are on schedule and normal operations will be resume at the end of next week, Lagoven said.
"The unit will be up and running again normally by the end of next week, as planned," Lagoven sources told Reuters.
The 108,000 bpd unit, which is used to produce gasoline, went down on October 20 following problems with an air compressor.

Last week PdVSA Vice President Claus Graf reiterated the unit would be up and running by the middle of November. In the interim, export contracts have been met from inventories at Amuay and the near-by Cordon and Curacao Isla refineries.
Venezuela is the U.S.'s top foreign gasoline supplier, shipping some 48,000 bpd over the first half of 1996, according to U.S. Department of Energy figures.
